# Running the Pipeline

## Launch

```bash
sbatch ChromSimPipe.sh
```

`ChromSimPipe.sh` follows the bagPipes / dietJuicer launcher pattern: it
sources the site's `profiles/<site>/env.sh` (software setup), builds a venv in
`env/` from `config/requirements.txt`, and runs Snakemake with that site's
profile (`hpcProfile` in the config). On `profiles/local`, run it with `bash`
instead of `sbatch`. Each rule becomes its own SLURM job.

## What happens

```
convertHic (per Hi-C sample)
getMotif ─► orientCTCF (per CTCF sample) ─► validateCTCF
    ─► simulateShard (condition × rep × shard, GPU)
        ─► mergeShards (condition × rep)
            ─► analyzeCondition (per condition) ─► benchmarkSummary
```

| Rule | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| `convertHic` | `hic2cool convert` `.hic` → `.cool` at `resolution` |
| `getMotif` | Downloads `ctcf_motif.jaspar_id` from JASPAR (skipped when `ctcf_motif.meme` is set) |
| `orientCTCF` | FIMO motif strand → oriented CTCF BED for the locus |
| `validateCTCF` | Checks every BED parses and maps onto the polymer |
| `simulateShard` | polychrom 3D loop-extrusion simulation (GPU) |
| `mergeShards` | Concatenates shard trajectories per replicate |
| `analyzeCondition` | Contact maps, P(s), insulation, APA, comparison with Hi-C |
| `benchmarkSummary` | Run time / memory of every job in one table |

Resources for each rule are in `profiles/<site>/config.yaml` under
`set-resources:`.

## Test run first

`config/ChromSimConfig.test.yaml` is the full config cut down to a cheap
end-to-end check: same samplesheet, locus and physics, but one condition, one
replicate, one shard, and 1,000 blocks instead of 50,000. It is 9 jobs, one of
them on a GPU, written to `output_test/`. Its results are a smoke test, not
data.

```bash
bash   ChromSimPipe.sh --configfile config/ChromSimConfig.test.yaml -n                     # dry run
sbatch ChromSimPipe.sh --configfile config/ChromSimConfig.test.yaml --until validateCTCF   # CPU steps only
sbatch ChromSimPipe.sh --configfile config/ChromSimConfig.test.yaml                        # one GPU simulation, end to end
```

Run it on every new cluster before a full run: it exercises environment
building, CTCF orientation, GPU access, and the analysis at a small fraction
of a full run's cost.

## Email notifications

Set an address and the workflow emails you once when it starts, once when it
finishes, and once if any job fails (not once per job):

```bash
export CHROMSIM_EMAIL=you@university.edu   # e.g. in ~/.bashrc
```

The address can also go in `notify: email:` in the config; the environment
variable keeps it out of a shared repo and wins if both are set.
`notify: events:` picks which of `start`, `success`, `error` to send, and
`notify: command:` is the shell command that sends one message (default
`mail -s {subject} {email}`; use e.g. `sendmail` on clusters without `mail`).
Check your cluster can send mail with
`echo test | mail -s test $CHROMSIM_EMAIL`. A failed email never fails the
workflow.

## Useful options

Extra arguments to `ChromSimPipe.sh` go straight to `snakemake`.

```bash
bash ChromSimPipe.sh -n                          # dry run
sbatch ChromSimPipe.sh --configfile other.yaml   # another (complete) config
sbatch ChromSimPipe.sh --until validateCTCF      # stop after CTCF setup
bash ChromSimPipe.sh --conda-create-envs-only    # build envs only (run on a compute node)
sbatch ChromSimPipe.sh --profile profiles/<site> # another compute site
```

### After a failed run

```bash
bash unlock.sh                    # release the Snakemake lock
sbatch ChromSimPipe.sh            # --rerun-incomplete is on by default
```

### Changing locus

Edit the `locus:` and `tiling:` blocks in the config (or write a new config
and pass it with `--configfile`), then resubmit. CTCF BED names include the
locus coordinates, so the workflow orients CTCF for the new window
automatically.

## Output structure

```
output/
├── {runName}_ChromSimSamplesheet.txt   # samplesheet with sample names
├── {runName}_benchmarking.tsv          # wall time / memory per job
├── mcool/{sample}.cool
├── motifs/{jaspar_id}.meme
├── ctcf/ctcf_oriented_{assembly}_{sample}_{chrom}_{start}_{end}.bed
├── sims/
│   ├── {params_name}_ctcf-{sample}_rep{N}_shard{M}/   # per-shard GPU output
│   └── merged_{params_name}_ctcf-{sample}_rep{N}/
├── analysis/{condition}/
├── logs/{rule}_{wildcards}.out|.err
├── logs_slurm/
├── benchmarks/{rule}_{wildcards}.tsv
└── done/                               # completion markers
```

## Monitoring

| Log | Path |
|-----|------|
| Launcher (main Snakemake process) | `ChromSimPipe-{jobid}.out` |
| Each job's stdout / stderr | `output/logs/{rule}_{wildcards}.out` / `.err` |
| SLURM job logs | `output/logs_slurm/` |

```bash
squeue -u $USER
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Snakemake lock error | `bash unlock.sh` then resubmit |
| `nvrtc: error: invalid value for --gpu-architecture` | The env has CUDA 13, which dropped Pascal/Volta GPUs; the env file pins CUDA 12.4, so rebuild the env on a compute node |
| `CUDA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PTX_VERSION` | The env's CUDA is newer than the node's driver supports (`nvidia-smi` shows the limit); lower `cuda-version` and rebuild |
| `convertHic` ends in `TIMEOUT` | Raise `convertHic: runtime:` in `profiles/<site>/config.yaml` |
| `no 'KR' normalization in ...cool` | Set `analysis.hic_balance` to a column it lists, or `False` |
| No emails arrive | Test `echo test \| mail -s test $CHROMSIM_EMAIL`; change `notify: command:` |
| Launcher job `OUT_OF_MEMORY` on the first run | Build the conda environments once on a compute node (`srun ... --mem=16g --pty bash`, then `bash ChromSimPipe.sh --conda-create-envs-only`) |
| A job failed | Read `output/logs/{rule}_{wildcards}.err` |
| Parameter changed but nothing reruns | Snakemake tracks the files in `output/done/`; delete the markers for the steps to redo |
